summary:
Catalunya stands under Spain's Ley 4/2023 on real and effective equality for trans persons and the guarantee of LGTBI rights, whose implementation in the region falls to the Generalitat de Catalunya, and under its own regional instrument, Ley 11/2014 of 10 October 2014, published in the Diari Oficial de la Generalitat de Catalunya on 17 October 2014.

Ley 11/2014 defines direct, indirect and association-based discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or sex characteristics. A trans visitor who is treated less favourably on those grounds within the region therefore has a regional statutory basis for complaint, and the statute's protections extend across education, health, employment and sport.

The statute guarantees partners in a same-sex relationship participation in death procedures concerning a partner, including identification of the body, burial and handling of personal effects.

Breaches are sanctionable under the statute. Article 35 sets minor infringements at between seven days' and three months' worth of the indicador de renda de suficiència de Catalunya, Article 38 places the sanctioning regime with the department competent for LGBTI non-discrimination, and the Síndic de Greuges is able to instigate proceedings.
tangentialFactors:
Catalunya's Ley de Parejas of 30 June 1998 was the first Spanish law to grant homosexual couples minimum legal provisions, placing the region ahead of the state framework on relationship recognition by seven years.

Ley 11/2014 was the autonomous statute after which the 2010s wave of Spanish regional LGTBI laws followed, so Catalan practice in this field has historically set the pattern for other autonomous communities rather than trailing them.
localsOnly:
Ley 11/2014 obliges Catalan public administrations to establish mechanisms so that administrative documentation reflects gender identity. The duty rests with the regional administration, and the sources do not describe how the mechanism operates in day-to-day practice.

The statute also broadened the Observatorio Catalán del Deporte so that it acts against violence and discrimination in sport, extending the region's anti-discrimination machinery into sporting settings used by residents.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources assembled for Catalunya record no incident of anti-trans violence in the region and no decided proceeding applying Ley 11/2014 on behalf of a trans complainant. Use of the statute's sanctioning regime in practice is unverified in the material available.

Whether the statute's protections are relied on by persons present in the region only briefly, such as visitors, is not addressed by the sources. Nor does any region-specific guidance on single-sex facilities or on screening practice at the region's airports appear in them.

The sources do not state whether the 1998 couples statute remains in force following later national and regional legislation.
